perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s available perspective:

- I work as a salesperson at a marketing firm with Katherine Lasiloo, the marketing manager. We have had differing opinions on traditional sales techniques versus digital marketing approaches.
- In a meeting room, I presented data and charts supporting traditional sales methods. I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed traditional methods were being overlooked. Katherine said the market is evolving and digital outreach has potential, then asked how I reconcile my data with rising online engagement. I said I did not want to abandon digital but felt proven methods were being sidelined. Katherine said she understood and suggested analyzing the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After that meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales. I felt uncertain and began questioning my support for only traditional methods. I asked her to explain how those strategies are developed. She said it involves targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making. I admitted my doubts and said I wanted to understand digital better. She welcomed my openness and suggested going deeper into the data.
- I proposed a joint strategy meeting to integrate traditional and digital marketing. Katherine agreed, said combining strengths could improve results, and suggested scheduling a brainstorm. I said I was hopeful and appreciated her willingness to collaborate. She said she looked forward to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After our joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime on a board presentation draft integrating both our ideas. I told Katherine about the draft. She reviewed it, said it looked comprehensive and well thought out, and noted my hard work. I thanked her and said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart. She agreed to review and fine-tune it once more.
- After our presentation and implementation of the new strategy, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our collaboration. I thanked Katherine and said I had learned a lot. She said it was a pleasure and credited my openness to new ideas. I proposed regular strategy sessions; she agreed, saying they would keep us on top of our game and market trends.
